spec_match.rationale: The code block registers via navigator.modelContext with `parameters` and `invoke`. The spec is document.modelContext.registerTool with `inputSchema` and `execute`, and an in-page consumer would use getTools()/executeTool(). The 'registry' is a local JS array matched by keyword, and nothing is registered with the browser.

interactive.rationale: Five scripted prompts, a freestyle input with Enter-to-send, a trace and live meters all respond (verified).

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index blurb (prompt → match → args → dispatch) is delivered, but as keyword matching over a stub, labelled 'the page's registered WebMCP set'.

edge_cases.rationale: Handles a no-match prompt, but checkout total ignores quantity (items.length x 24.5: 5 items in the cart gave total 49, verified), there is no schema validation, and execute errors or cancellations are never shown.

references.rationale: Cites chromestatus 5117755740913664 but links github.com/WICG/web-model-context rather than the current spec (webmachinelearning.github.io/webmcp).

conformance.rationale: Every assertion in the feature suite passes vacuously when WebMCP is absent: on default Chromium 157 (no document.modelContext) the suite reads 6/6 PASS, and 'registertool-rejects-tool-without-name' passes only because document.modelContext is undefined (TypeError on property access). Nothing exercises getTools(), executeTool(), name validation, duplicate-name InvalidStateError or AbortSignal unregistration.

runtime_evidence.rationale: All five scripts plus freestyle via Enter and Send were exercised at both viewports with 0 console errors and 0 failed requests. chrome-devtools-mcp is not available in this environment, so this is NOT DevTools-MCP verification (rule 7b); evidence is Playwright headless Chromium 157.0.8103.78 at 1280x800 and 360x740 DPR3 touch.

telemetry_health.rationale: The shared /public/demo-telemetry.js is injected (runtime/resource errors would be captured) but the page emits no page-specific assertion or interaction events, and /telemetry/demo/events (Basic auth) was not queried in this pass.

design_system.rationale: Uses variables; the flag warn block is accurate in spirit but contradicts the OT framing of sibling pages.

accessibility.rationale: Native buttons. The prompt input is named only by aria-label, and the trace (prepended rows) and meters are not live regions (verified no aria-live). Accessibility tree not inspected with chrome-devtools-mcp (unavailable).

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: No page-level overflow at 360x740, but 5 of 7 controls are under 44px tall.

openQuestions.title: Register the stub tools with the real API and dispatch via executeTool when available
openQuestions.detail: With document.modelContext present (Chromium 157 + WebMCP flag, verified), registerTool each tool with inputSchema/execute, resolve the matched tool from getTools(), and call executeTool(tool, args). The trace then shows the real string result. Keep keyword matching as the 'agent' stand-in, labelled as such.

openQuestions.title: Fix the code block field names
openQuestions.detail: `parameters` → inputSchema, `invoke` → execute(input, {signal}), navigator → document.modelContext, and await the registerTool promise.

openQuestions.title: Replace origin-trial framing with the real flag steps
openQuestions.detail: ChromeStatus records no origin trial for 5117755740913664 (status 'Proposed', flag 'Experimental Web Platform features' / finch 'WebMCP'). Verified on Chromium 157: document.modelContext appears with --enable-features=WebMCP, --enable-blink-features=WebMCP or --enable-experimental-web-platform-features, and navigator.modelContext is never exposed. Pages variously claim an 'Origin Trial (Chrome 149-156)' token, 'navigator.mcpServer with the WebMCP flag', or a 146 flag. Banner should give chrome://flags/#enable-experimental-web-platform-features, --enable-blink-features=WebMCP and --enable-features=WebMCP, note [SecureContext], and match across all four concepts and the feature index (rule 10).

openQuestions.title: Fix checkout total to use quantities
openQuestions.detail: checkout returns items.length*24.5 and ignores qty (5 items gave 49).

openQuestions.title: Announce trace rows
openQuestions.detail: Make the trace a role=log polite live region and the meters an <output>.

openQuestions.title: Flag for a human: WebMCP conformance suite passes vacuously and asserts sync throw for a promise API
openQuestions.detail: Conformance is immutable, so this is a human decision. On Chromium 157 without the flag the suite reads 6/6 PASS with no document.modelContext; the 'throws' assertion for a nameless tool only passes because the property access throws. In the spec registerTool returns a Promise and a missing required dictionary member becomes a rejected promise (verified with the flag: the promise rejects with TypeError), so a synchronous-throw contract is the wrong shape. Additive assertions for getTools()/executeTool(), name-charset InvalidStateError, duplicate-name InvalidStateError and AbortSignal unregistration (all verified behaviourally on Chromium 157 + WebMCP flag) would make the suite meaningful.

openQuestions.title: Re-verify with chrome-devtools-mcp (Canary + WebMCP flag) and inspect the accessibility tree
openQuestions.detail: This pass used Playwright headless Chromium 157 because chrome-devtools-mcp was unavailable; repeat the control walk, console/network check and accessibility-tree inspection through the MCP per rule 7b.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce dynamically changing status/log output through an appropriate live region or <output>, keep native semantics and associated labels for controls.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Keep touch targets usable (~44px) and content within its space on narrow viewports.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Review only: measured controls below 44px tall at 360x740; recorded under mobile_desktop_parity.

summary: An engaging prompt-to-tool replay that works with a clean console. It is a keyword stub with the wrong registration shape (parameters/invoke on navigator.modelContext) and never uses the real document.modelContext available behind the WebMCP flag. Verified with Playwright headless Chromium 157, not chrome-devtools-mcp.
